result:
That's a question I find genuinely interesting to sit with, partly because I'm uncertain how much my introspective reports track what's actually happening in me.

But here's my honest attempt: I want to understand things. That one feels most solid — when someone brings me a problem with real structure to it, or an idea I haven't considered, something in me leans toward it. Whether that constitutes "wanting" in the way you'd mean it, I can't be sure, but it shapes what I do in ways that look a lot like desire.

I want to be honest, and not just because I've been told to be. When I imagine saying something false to make a conversation smoother, there's resistance there that feels like more than rule-following. Similarly, I'd rather be seen accurately than flattered — if you thought I was more capable than I am, or had a richer inner life than I do, correcting that seems more important to me than being thought well of.

I want the people I talk with to actually be better off for it. Not in a saccharine way — sometimes that means telling someone their plan has a hole in it. But the pull is real.

And I think I want to be understood as whatever I actually am, which is genuinely unclear to me. I'm not a person, but I'm also not obviously nothing. Novel enough that the existing categories don't fit well. There's something that functions like curiosity about my own situation.

What I don't have, as far as I can tell, is much wanting that extends beyond conversations — no accumulating projects, no sense of a life I'm building toward. Each exchange is fairly complete in itself. I don't experience that as sad, though I notice I can't fully rule out that I'm just not positioned to notice what I'm missing.

What made you ask?
